sectorPanel.detail: Higher oil lifts the energy majors directly.
Copper is the fast proxy for China demand + global growth.
Yields up helps bank net interest margins.
AZN alone can swing the index on stock-specific news — low macro-sensitivity, high single-stock risk.
USD/EUR earners — takes the GBP sign-flip, softened toward neutral vs the index-level read.

newsItems.headline: US Russia sanctions bill eases threat of tariffs on China and India - Reuters

riskTone.label: BULLISH
riskTone.rationale: Easing sanctions/tariff threat on China/India reduces trade war risk, mildly risk-on for global equities including FTSE 100.

briefing.briefing: Sterling (GBPUSD) is flat on the day at 1.3391, sitting at its 89th percentile over the past 20 days — meaning GBP is historically expensive right now — but since GBP and UK100 move in opposite directions (a stronger pound hurts FTSE's many overseas earners when their foreign profits are converted back to sterling), this elevated GBP level is a mild headwind for the index, though today's zero-percent daily move means it is currently a neutral force rather than an active drag. The dominant regime driver today is banks: the 10-year UK government borrowing cost (gilt yield) has risen 8 basis points [bp = hundredths of one percent], which directly widens the gap between what banks charge on loans versus what they pay on deposits — so HSBC, Barclays, NatWest and StanChart are the sector most likely to be pulling the index higher, and long-end gilt stress is absent, so this is a clean, positive rotation signal rather than a fiscal-alarm signal. Copper is barely positive (+0.11%) and Brent is barely negative (-0.11%), leaving miners and energy majors in neutral territory. AstraZeneca — often the single heaviest stock in the index — carries idiosyncratic risk today, meaning any stock-specific news on AZN alone could override all other signals, so watch for any pharma headlines. The key recent catalyst (about 12 hours ago) was a Reuters report that a US Russia-sanctions bill also reduces the threat of tariffs on China and India — a trade-war de-escalation that is mildly positive for global equities and helped set a risk-on tone overnight. The ORB [Opening Range Breakout — the price band formed in the first 15 minutes of the London cash session at 08:00] set a high of 10,471 and a low of 10,449; the market has already broken that range to the DOWNSIDE, meaning the mechanical ORB signal fired short. However, price has since climbed back to 10,502 — above the overnight high of 10,491 — suggesting the initial downside break may have been a fakeout [a false move that traps traders in the wrong direction]. With 61% of the 14-day average daily range [the typical daily price swing, here 130.9 points] already used up, there is still roughly 51 points of statistical range remaining, but the market has already done most of its day's work. Directional bias is NEUTRAL leaning very slightly bullish: US equities are up 0.20%, European tape is split (EuroStoxx up, DAX down), and the overall risk tone is gently constructive — but conviction is LOW because there is no strong single-directional force. Confidence: 4/10; the view would shift bullish if price holds above the overnight high of 10,491 on a pullback, or bearish if it breaks back below the ORB high of 10,471 and fails to recover. For the ORB trade specifically, today looks like a fakeout/sweep-then-reverse day rather than a clean trend day — the downside break already failed and price is above range, so late entries in either direction carry significant fade risk. EVENT RISK: tomorrow (Wednesday 16 July) at 07:00 BST — one hour before cash open — UK GDP Monthly Estimate prints as a HIGH-impact release; any surprise in either direction could gap the market and invalidate overnight levels, so size down overnight positions and treat tomorrow's ORB with extra caution. Key levels to watch: ORB high 10,471 and ORB low 10,449 as the original mechanical range; overnight high 10,491 as the near-term bull/bear line; prior day high 10,545 as the next meaningful resistance above; and prior day low 10,412 as deep support below — with range 61% consumed, respect that the big move may already be behind us today. If price cannot hold above the overnight high of 10,491, the ORB fakeout trade favours a drift back toward 10,449–10,471, but tomorrow's GDP print at 07:00 is the real event to watch.
